content:
The Akademies under the Ministry of Culture
celebrated the 80th Independence Day with patriotic fervour
through a wide range of cultural and participatory activities under the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign. Across the country, the celebrations included Tiranga rallies and yatras, flag-hoisting ceremonies, mass singing of
Vande Mataram
, patriotic theatre and musical performances, art and painting workshops, wall paintings, clay modelling, traditional crafts, exhibitions and student-centric activities. These initiatives brought together students, artists, cultural practitioners and citizens, showcasing India’s rich
cultural diversity and spirit of unity in diversity
, while fostering patriotism, national pride and collective participation and commemorating
150 years of
Vande Mataram
.
The
National School of Drama (NSD)
and its centres across the country engaged citizens and students through a range of programmes celebrating the spirit of Har Ghar Tiranga and the 80th Independence Day. NSD created awareness about the celebrations and the 150th year of
Vande Mataram
through its social media and other communication platforms, while sensitising citizens about the proper display of the National Flag and encouraging participation in the
‘Selfie with Tiranga’ initiative
. More than
250 NSDians uploaded their selfies
on the portal. NSD also conducted a mass singing of
Vande Mataram
at its campus and organised a
rally of around 400 participants in the Mandi House area
on 14 August. On 15 August, an interaction programme on patriotism for students was organised at the NSD Delhi campus.
Across its regional centres, NSD Bengaluru organised a
bike rally
and
three plays
on patriotism. The NSD TIE Centre, Tripura, conducted a procession promoting Har Ghar Tiranga, collaborated with the Lalit Kala Akademi on a Tiranga-themed wall-painting project and organised a cultural programme. The NSD Varanasi Centre organised a rally with
Rang Sangeet
and patriotic performances, while the NSD Sikkim Centre also conducted programmes to mark the occasion. In Srinagar, NSD’s first-year students joined Kashmiri artists at Lal Mandi on 14 August for
Watan Ke Rang, Kashmir Ke Sang
, featuring theatre, Kashmiri folk dances, Bhand Pather and Lal Ded Vak, opening with
Vande Mataram
and concluding with
Jana Gana Mana
.
The
Sahitya Akademi
participated in the nationwide celebrations through
Tiranga Yatras, Tiranga Selfie activities, Tricolour illumination and decoration
of its premises, and mass singing of
Vande Mataram
. It also observed
Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Diwas at Hansraj College, University of Delhi
, with around 200 students participating. The programme recalled the suffering, displacement and human cost associated with Partition while encouraging young people to engage with this chapter of the nation’s history and reinforcing the values of peace, harmony, mutual respect and national unity. Through these activities, the Akademi highlighted the role of literature and cultural engagement in strengthening citizens’ connection with the nation.
The
Sangeet Natak Akademi
presented a
five-segment thematic musical programme
showcasing folk and traditional musical heritage from Chhattisgarh and Bastar, Maharashtra, Goa and Madhya Pradesh. The presentation opened with
Mangal Dhun
and moved through community celebration rhythms of Maharashtra, the festive traditions of Goa’s Konkan coast and indigenous musical traditions of Madhya Pradesh. It culminated in a finale bringing together musicians and instruments from all four regions, conveying the message of
“Unity in Diversity”
. The Akademi also arranged a traditional musical welcome for dignitaries featuring Tasha, Tutari, Dhol and Shank.
The
Lalit Kala Akademi
celebrated Independence Day through visual arts activities, rallies, workshops and public participation programmes across its headquarters and Regional Centres. At its headquarters in New Delhi, the Akademi, in association with the Sahitya Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi, organised the
‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ programme
and
flag hoisting at Rabindra Bhawan
on 13 August 2026. The programme was followed by a Tiranga Rally in which more than 1,500 participants, including schoolchildren, working artists, art enthusiasts and local residents, participated.
Its Regional Centres also organised a range of activities. At Agartala, a student rally and wall-painting programme were organised at Nazrul Kala Kshetra, involving students and senior artists. At Shimla, a
Tricolour Rally
was organised on 13 August with students of PM Shri Kendriya Vidyalaya Jakhoo Hills and Jawaharlal Nehru Fine Arts College, Shimla, along with a painting workshop at the Lalit Kala Akademi Art Gallery, Gaiety Theatre.
The Regional Centre, Ahmedabad,
organised a Tiranga Rally and Clay Modelling Workshop
on 15 August under the theme
“Viksit Bharat 2047 – Mitti Se Bharat”
, with around 15 schoolchildren participating. At Kolkata, the Regional Centre organised the Har Ghar Tiranga programme, an art workshop and a sit-and-draw programme, with
more than 1,000 school students and 300 working artists
, college students and art enthusiasts participating, followed by a
Tiranga Rally involving more than 1,500 participants
. Flag-hoisting ceremonies were also held at both campuses on 15 August, with the buildings illuminated in Tricolour lights.
The
Lucknow Regional Centre
organised a
Children’s Painting Workshop
on 12 August, followed by a
Tiranga Rally
on 13 August in which approximately
1,500 people participated
, as well as a patriotic cultural programme. A flag-hoisting ceremony was also held at the Centre on 15 August. The
Chennai Regional Centre
observed Independence Day with a flag-hoisting ceremony attended by staff members, artists and art lovers.
The
Kalakshetra Foundation
observed the
Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026
across its four units through educational, artistic and participatory activities. The campaign included
pledges, Tricolour illumination, flag distribution, Tricolour-themed decoration and mass singing
of
Vande Mataram
and the National Anthem by students and staff. Students participated in rangoli, art-from-waste, clay modelling, vegetable carving and salad-making using Tricolour themes, as well as presentations on
Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat
.
The Foundation also undertook traditional craft activities including
Tricolour weaving, natural dyeing, Kalamkari work and making of flags and Tricolour-themed crafts
. The celebrations featured a puppet show on unsung heroes, women warriors and freedom fighters, a fancy-dress competition on national leaders and freedom fighters, and rallies and public exhibitions, bringing together students, teachers, artists, craftspeople and members of the public. The campaign
culminated in the 80th Independence Day celebrations on 15 August 2026
.
Through the collective efforts of the Akademies, the celebrations brought the spirit of
Har Ghar Tiranga
into cultural spaces across the country. From theatre and music to painting, literature, traditional crafts and community participation, the programmes provided diverse platforms for citizens, particularly young people, to connect with the values of patriotism, national pride and cultural heritage. The celebrations also commemorated
150 years of
Vande Mataram
while showcasing the many artistic traditions that contribute to India’s cultural identity. Through these nationwide initiatives, the Akademies reaffirmed the message of
unity in diversity and a shared commitment to the nation
.

title: ‘Raksha Shakti’ key to achieving the goal of Viksit Bharat, says Prime Minister in his 2026 Independence Day address
subtitle:
India must become global supplier of next-gen defence tech: Shri Narendra Modi

Need to focus on indigenous defence equipment & enhancing military capabilities in present evolving times: PM

Work on Mission Sudarshan Chakra progressing rapidly: Prime Minister

Huge voluntary force of civil defence to be created to overcome modern challenges: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 AUG 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
‘Raksha Shakti’ is among the seven streams of power outlined by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in his 2026 Independence Day address to the nation, as key to building a Viksit Bharat by 2047. From the ramparts of the Red Fort in Delhi on August 15, 2026, the Prime Minister emphasised the need for Aatmanirbharta in defence and called for India to emerge as a global supplier of next-generation defence technologies.
“There is no alternative to being self-reliant in defence. When countries around the world are increasingly thinking about their own interests, Bharat cannot simply remain a market for the world. We must develop drones and counter-drone systems, and take leadership in hypersonic defence technologies,” said the Prime Minister.
Reiterating the Government’s resolve to realise the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Shri Narendra Modi asserted that the nation should no longer live by depending on other countries. “There may be many things available in the world that are cheaper and can be obtained more quickly. But relying on them does not build our own capabilities, nor does it test the strength of our capabilities. Therefore, we must strengthen our own capacities and protect our own interests ourselves. That is why we are moving forward with a firm resolve for ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’. The hearts of Indians are connecting with initiatives like Make in India, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local,” he said.
The Prime Minister added that cybersecurity is also an area of defence where the nation can harness the capabilities of the youth for the benefit of the country and the world.
Shri Narendra Modi underscored the need to focus on indigenous defence equipment while enhancing the capabilities of the defence forces to stay prepared in the current changing times. “The nature of warfare is changing today; there is no longer a guarantee that conflict will be confined to the borders. Modern warfare can target refineries, the banking sector, or data centers, in a sense, a new form of combat where infrastructure and factories are being destroyed. We announced ‘Mission Sudarshan Chakra’ some years ago, and work on it is progressing rapidly,” he said.
Highlighting the transformation witnessed in the defence sector in the last 12 years, the Prime Minister stated that defence production has increased nearly fourfold. He added that defence exports have risen by almost 50 times, with Indian weapons reaching about 100 countries. “Whether the challenge is within or beyond the borders, India is prepared for any situation… India’s reputation is gradually increasing on the global stage,” he said.
Shri Narendra Modi emphasised that building a secure India is the responsibility of every citizen, called for enhanced preparedness to deal with emerging threats. “The civil defence systems that have developed in our country in accordance with the wars of the last century have become outdated. In the coming days, we will create a vibrant network of civil defence. We will familiarise them with modern systems. We are going to create a huge voluntary force of civil defence to overcome modern challenges,” he said.
The Prime Minister also highlighted the growing role of Nari Shakti in nation-building, including in the Defence Forces. “Our daughters graduating from the NDA are demonstrating the capability to lead the nation’s military with great confidence and authority,” he said.

title: DLI Scheme-backed Chip Design Startup - Aheesa Digital Innovations Achieved First-Pass Silicon Success With ‘VIHAAN’, a Broadband Chip Built Using the Indigenous VEGA Microprocessor
subtitle:
VIHAAN Aims to Bring Fibre Broadband to Indian Homes and Has Attracted VC Funding from the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Fund Management Corporation (TNIFMC) and Other Investors

DLI Scheme-backed Companies Have Cumulatively Raised Over $100 Million in VC Funding and Achieved 35 Design Tape-outs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 AUG 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Semiconductor chip design is a critical value driver across the semiconductor value chain, contributing up to 50% of overall value addition and accounting for approximately 15–35% of the Bill of Materials (BOM) cost of electronic products.
Recognising the pivotal role of semiconductor design in the country’s strategic technological ambitions, the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme is supporting Indian Startups for designing chips for a wide range of strategic and commercial applications. These include satellite communications, drones, surveillance cameras, Defence and Aerospace Systems, Automotive, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, LED drivers, AI systems, Telecom Equipment, and Smart Meters.
Aheesa Digital Innovations
Headquartered in Chennai, Aheesa is an Indian fabless semiconductor startup that designs chips for broadband networking and security. Taped out on Republic Day and achieving first-pass silicon success on Independence Day this year, ‘VIHAAN’ - a networking System-on-Chip (SoC) purpose-built for Fibre Broadband- will now proceed towards production tape-out, targeted for 2027.
As India expands its digital infrastructure through optical fibre, 5G, and broadband-led services, the need for domestically designed semiconductor solutions is growing. Aheesa, through its VIHAAN series, successive funding milestones, and active support from the DLI Scheme, is positioned to serve this need.
Investor Confidence - Supporting India’s Deep-Tech Innovation to Scale Global Solutions
Earlier this year, Aheesa raised about ₹40 crore from TNIFMC through the Tamil Nadu Emerging Sector Seed Fund (TNESSF) and other private investors to accelerate product development and support the company’s growth in the semiconductor space. These successive rounds of funding after approval under the DLI Scheme reflects growing confidence of investors in Aheesa's ability to deliver advanced broadband silicon solutions from India.
Government support helping Indian chip companies move from idea to product
Aheesa’s achievement is part of a larger transformation taking place in India’s semiconductor design ecosystem. Through the Government’s semiconductor programmes, state-of-the-art chip-design tools made available to 455 organisations, including 350 academic institutions and 105 startups, enabling students, researchers and companies across the country to design chips.
Companies supported under the DLI Scheme have cumulatively achieved over 30 chip design tape-outs across various foundries and raised more than US$100 million in VC funding, demonstrating growing investor confidence in India’s semiconductor design capabilities. Under the Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme, 245 chip designs have been taped out by 71 academic institutions, to meet future workforce requirements.
Other recent successes under the Scheme
1.
Vervesemi Microelectronics
achieved first-pass silicon success
of BLDC Motor Controller chip using indigenous microprocessor by Incore Semiconductor and its Motor Driver chip.
2. Netrasemi
successfully tested 12nm Vision SoC with integrated video analytics acceleration.
3.
OptoML
received its 12nm ‘compute-in-memory’ SoC, which makes AI processing faster and power-efficient.
4. Mindgrove Technologies
announced a partnership with PRAMA India to explore the usage of its Vision SoC in CCTV surveillance cameras.
5.
IndieSemiC
secured global certification for its Bluetooth (BLE 6) chip module.
Building an Indian semiconductor ecosystem
The Government’s semiconductor initiatives are aimed not merely at designing individual chips, but at building an ecosystem covering the entire semiconductor value chain — from chip design and manufacturing to advanced packaging, equipment, materials, research and development, and skilled manpower. With Semicon 2.0, approved with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore in July 2026, India is taking this effort to the next level, with the objective of building a globally competitive semiconductor ecosystem.
The progress of companies such as Aheesa Digital Innovations demonstrates that Indian semiconductor designs are increasingly moving beyond the laboratory. Chips designed in India are now being fabricated, tested, validated, and prepared for customer trials. As the ecosystem matures, silicon-validated designs will move towards volume manufacturing, positioning Indian companies as credible global suppliers while strengthening domestic supply chains and self-reliance.

title: Union Minister Shri Jual Oram and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, Jointly Release National Framework and Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs
subtitle: Twin publications, translate a nationwide consultative exercise covering 217 ITDAs/ITDPs across 19 States/UTs into an actionable reform roadmap for last-mile tribal development delivery
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 AUG 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, today jointly released two important publications of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs — the “
National Framework for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs
” and the “
Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs.
” The two documents mark the culmination of a comprehensive, consultative and evidence-based national exercise aimed at strengthening Integrated Tribal Development Agencies and Projects (ITDAs/ITDPs), the principal field-level institutions driving tribal development across the country.
The publications were released in the presence of Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Shri Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officers of the Ministry.
Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted that ITDAs/ITDPs have historically served as a critical bridge between government programmes and tribal communities, and that their role has grown even more significant with the scale of interventions under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and PM-JANMAN.
Dr. Balasubramaniam noted that the principles of ranking, real-time data-driven monitoring and convergence that delivered saturation of outcomes in under-developed districts and blocks now stand embedded in the ITDA/ITDP reform architecture. He observed that evidence-based administrative attention can transform lagging regions, these publications seek to replicate that model within the tribal development ecosystem, using ITDAs as the delivery vehicle for saturation of entitlements at the last mile.
The exercise was undertaken under the overall guidance and vision of Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Smt. Ranjana Chopra, whose emphasis on evidence-based, field-driven institutional reform shaped the design of the entire consultative process. Smt. Chopra’s consistent direction to move beyond a one-size-fits-all approach and build context-specific, accountable
field institutions provided the strategic anchor for the Ministry’s roadmap for strengthening ITDAs and ITDPs across the country.
The Ministry had initiated this exercise in April 2026, covering 214 ITDAs/ITDPs across 17 States/UTs, through a standardised assessment involving Project Officers, State Tribal Welfare Departments and Tribal Research Institutes. Designed as a bottom-up, consultative exercise rather than a desk-based study, it included State-level workshops, field visits and direct consultations, allowing ground-level challenges and successful practices to shape the national roadmap. The exercise culminated in the Evidence-Weighted ITDA Diagnostic Scoring Framework, assessing institutions across 15 parameters spanning five institutional domains.
To operationalize this exercise on the ground, structured consultative workshops were conducted across States/UTs in April and May 2026, led by Dr. Varnali Deka, Director, DAJGUA Division and Shri Jafar Malik, Deputy Secretary, EMRS. The officers engaged directly with all ITDA/ITDP Project Officers and State Tribal Research Institutes to understand institutional status, collate ground-level data, followed by detailed validation exercise to ensure that the diagnostic exercise remained firmly rooted in field realities. These findings were then analyzed to create a national framework, roadmap and a set of operational guidelines.
This exercise reached a major milestone on 3rd June 2026, when the Ministry convened the National Conclave on Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, graced by the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu.
The National Framework provides the assessment methodology and strategic direction, while the Operational Guidelines translate these recommendations into practical measures relating to institutional restructuring, convergence, evidence-based planning, digital governance, outcome-based monitoring and capacity building. For the first time, a common institutional assessment methodology has been made available to States, enabling each ITDA to identify its gaps and prepare a Performance Improvement Roadmap suited to its own context.
Shri Jual Oram said the objective is not merely to rank institutions but to build a culture of continuous institutional improvement, and urged States to undertake State-level reviews with all ITDA/ITDP Project Officers, prepare institution-specific action plans and establish quarterly monitoring of institutional performance, on the lines of the district and block-level monitoring cadence followed under ADP and ABP.
The Minister recommended strengthening the ITDA/ITDP ecosystem through a more efficient fund-flow mechanism, including exploring direct transfer of funds to ITDAs; augmenting technical manpower for better project execution; and institutionalizing regular Governing Council meetings with active participation of PRI representatives and senior State leadership to improve convergence, accountability and implementation.
Both dignitaries congratulated the States, Project Officers, Tribal Research Institutes and Ministry officials whose field experience shaped the two publications.

title: Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India launches RSVC-AMRIT platform developed by NABARD to strengthen rural innovation and technology transfer
ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 AUG 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, launched the RSVC AMRIT platform on 15th August 2025, the 80th Independence Day, marking a significant step towards strengthening technology-led rural development. Developed by NABARD in collaboration with the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (OPSA) to the Government of India, AMRIT serves as the digital backbone of the RuTAGe Smart Village Centre (RSVC) ecosystem, supporting rural innovation and technology transfer and enabling wider adoption of appropriate technologies in rural areas. The launch event was attended by Dr. Shaji Krishnan V., Chairman, NABARD, along with representatives from various organisations and stakeholder groups.
In his address, Prof. Sood emphasised that AMRIT is designed as a comprehensive digital ecosystem supporting the complete RSVC lifecycle, from technology discovery and validation to deployment tracking, collaboration, monitoring and knowledge management. He said the platform will progressively bring together innovators, technology providers, startups, validators, accelerators, implementation partners, funding agencies, academic institutions and rural communities on a shared platform. By connecting these stakeholders, AMRIT is expected to strengthen collaboration and accelerate the dissemination of technologies in rural areas, helping take technology and innovation closer to the last mile.
Highlighting the need for the platform, Dr. Krishnan noted that while India has a rich ecosystem of scientific institutions, innovators, startups and technology providers, connecting appropriate technologies with rural needs remains a challenge. AMRIT seeks to bridge this gap by connecting rural needs with innovations, institutions and implementation mechanisms, strengthening technology dissemination and adoption at the grassroots level. He reaffirmed NABARD’s commitment to supporting such enterprises across the country, in addition to the 8 RSVCs currently being supported.
The RSVC initiative facilitates the transfer of appropriate and affordable technologies from research institutions, innovators and startups to rural communities through village-level technology hubs, covering areas such as agriculture, rural enterprises, renewable energy, education, assistive technologies, water and sanitation, and citizen services. AMRIT builds on this physical outreach by adding a digital layer to the ecosystem, with NABARD expecting it to evolve into a national repository of rural innovations, technologies, best practices and collaboration opportunities, supporting wider technology adoption and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The initiative builds on NABARD’s earlier tripartite MoU with OPSA and NABFOUNDATION, a subsidiary of NABARD, and the establishment of a Centre of Excellence on RSVCs at its head office in Mumbai. On the occasion, NABARD shared the broad contours of its scheme for establishing RSVCs, which will be supported by NABARD and set up in collaboration with corporates through CSR initiatives, with NABFOUNDATION serving as the implementation partner.

title: Lokpal of India Celebrates 80th Independence Day; Reaffirms Commitment to Clean and Corruption-Free Governance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 AUG 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day of India, the National flag was hoisted by Hon’ble Shri Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, Chairperson, Lokpal of India in the august presence of Hon’ble Members: Shri Justice Lingappa Narayana Swamy, Shri Justice Sanjay Yadav, Shri Sushil Chandra, Shri justice Ritu Raj Awasthi, Shri Pankaj Kumar and Shri Ajay Tirkey. He extended greetings of Independence Day to all Hon’ble Members, senior officers, staff and their family members.
Recalling the inspiring words of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, he emphasized the vision of a nation “where the mind is without fear and the head is held high.” Citizens were urged to reaffirm this ideal and uphold it in thought and action.
The address highlighted that India’s freedom is hard-earned, achieved through the immense sacrifices of freedom fighters and countless patriots whose courage continues to inspire future generations. The hoisting of the National Flag was described as not merely a ceremonial act but a solemn reminder of both the nation’s past and the responsibilities that accompany freedom. He stressed that true freedom means freedom from hunger, injustice, oppression, and inequality, and the opportunity for every citizen to live with dignity.
Special emphasis was laid on the role of the Lokpal of India as an institution committed to clean, and corruption free governance. The increasing number of complaints received by the Lokpal was viewed as a sign of growing citizen engagement and confidence in the institution.
He reaffirmed the Lokpal’s commitment to the Constitution, the rule of law, accountability, efficiency, transparency, and accessibility. He called for an institution that is efficient, transparent, accessible, and strengthened through the effective use of technology. He emphasised on the Lokpal’s fundamental purpose to serve the Constitution, to uphold the rule of law and to ensure that public authority is exercised with responsibility. All officials were urged to treat every complaint with seriousness, fairness, and objectivity, remembering that behind every file is a citizen seeking justice and a life affected by institutional decisions.
He concluded his speech by expressing sincere gratitude to the Hon’ble Members, officers, staff, and their families for their dedication and professionalism and thanked everyone for participating in the celebration. The speech ended with a patriotic call of “Jai Hind”.
